findings.title: Per-target output dir derived from config stem can silently collide and clobber another target's artifacts
findings.description: `_safe_target_name(config_path)` returns `config_path.stem.replace('.', '-')` and is used as the per-target output subdirectory in `_run_target` (`target_dir = output_dir / _safe_target_name(target.config_path)`), which is then `shutil.rmtree`'d and recreated on each run. Target uniqueness, however, is only enforced on the full `config_path` and on `name` (`_load_target_specs` lines 204-207), never on the derived directory name. Two distinct config filenames can map to the same `_safe_target_name`, in which case the second target's run deletes (rmtree) and overwrites the first target's artifacts within the same output_dir, silently losing one target's results while both appear in the manifest.
findings.evidence: stem of 'cosmic-ray.registry.toml' is 'cosmic-ray.registry' -> replace('.','-') -> 'cosmic-ray-registry'. Adversarial example: 'cosmic-ray.a.b.toml' -> stem 'cosmic-ray.a.b' -> 'cosmic-ray-a-b', and 'cosmic-ray.a-b.toml' -> stem 'cosmic-ray.a-b' -> 'cosmic-ray-a-b' collide. _load_target_specs only checks `len(set(names)) != len(names)` and `len(set(configs)) != len(configs)` (configs = config_path list), so the collision passes validation. In _run_target: `if target_dir.exists(): shutil.rmtree(target_dir)` then both targets write target-summary.json/session files into the identical directory.

findings.title: Spurious 'survival rate could not be parsed' failure appended when a critical stage aborts before the rate stage runs
findings.description: In `_run_target`, when a critical stage other than `baseline` aborts the loop early (the `break` at line 562-563 fires for `init`/`filter-pragma`/`exec`), `session.sqlite` already exists (it is created by `init`) but the `rate` stage never executes, so `rate.txt` is never written. `_parse_survival_rate` then returns None because the file does not exist. The guard at line 580 is `if session_file.exists() and survival_rate is None:` which is satisfied, so an additional failure string 'survival rate could not be parsed from rate.txt' is appended on top of the genuine '<stage> exited with code N' failure. The recorded failure reason is factually wrong (the rate was never attempted, not unparseable), producing misleading diagnostics in target-summary.json, mutation-summary.json/.md and the printed summary for a gate whose entire purpose is clear correctness signal.
findings.evidence: Loop at 550-563: on `exec` returncode != 0, appends 'exec exited with code N' and `break`s (exec is in the critical set). `session_file` = target_dir/'session.sqlite' was created by the earlier `init` stage (cmd at line 514). `rate` stage (line 536-541, writes rate.txt) is never reached. Line 384-385 `_parse_survival_rate`: `if not rate_path.exists(): return None`. Line 580: `if session_file.exists() and survival_rate is None:` -> True -> failures gains a second, inaccurate entry.

findings.title: Duplicated 'format rate as percent or n/a' logic with inconsistent defensiveness
findings.description: The optional-rate-to-string formatting exists twice with diverging behavior. `_format_optional_rate` (lines 454-457) guards with `isinstance(value, int | float)` and returns 'n/a' otherwise, while `_write_summary_markdown` (lines 432-433) inlines `'n/a' if survival is None else f'{survival:.2f}%'` / `'n/a' if fail_over is None else f'{fail_over:.2f}%'`, which assumes the value is strictly float-or-None and would raise on any non-numeric, non-None value. The markdown writer could reuse `_format_optional_rate` for a single, consistently-defensive implementation.
findings.evidence: _format_optional_rate: `if isinstance(value, int | float): return f'{float(value):.2f}%'` else `'n/a'`. _write_summary_markdown: `survival_text = 'n/a' if survival is None else f'{survival:.2f}%'` and `fail_over_text = 'n/a' if fail_over is None else f'{fail_over:.2f}%'` — same '%.2f%% or n/a' intent, different None-vs-isinstance handling.
findings.est_reduction: ~3-4 lines; removes a second, less-robust formatter
findings.behavior_preservation: Behavior-preserving for the only values actually produced (survival_rate/fail_over are float|None); reusing _format_optional_rate additionally hardens the markdown path against unexpected types instead of raising.

findings.title: Injected quotes() api_input fixture hand-rolls (and has drifted from) the shared load_v2_api_source helper, embedding a latent config-path bug
findings.description: The _QUOTES_API_INPUT_BLOCK string is appended verbatim into the scaffolded rating/main.py as the body of the `quotes` api_input node. It hand-rolls the v2 per-port cache resolution: it manually computes _json_cache_dir for the 'working' then 'committed' layer, calls is_per_port_cache_valid twice, raises the stale-cache RuntimeError, derives _emit_labels, calls load_per_port_cache, and branches single-vs-multi return. This is exactly (and only) what the shared runtime/codegen helper haute._json_shred.load_v2_api_source already does (src/haute/_json_shred.py:968-1023). Production codegen for an api_input JSON node (_api_input_template, src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:234-249) now emits just `return load_v2_api_source(str(_data_path), _v2_config)` precisely so 'this generated/deploy path can't drift from the runtime builder'. The harness fixture has drifted: it duplicates ~37 lines of logic instead of calling the helper, so it can silently diverge from the real codec and stop faithfully exercising it. Worse, in copying the old logic it introduced a config-path-resolution defect: it uses `_config_path = Path("config/quote_input/quotes.json")` (a CWD-relative path), whereas production codegen uses `_config_path = Path(__file__).parent / {config_path_repr}` (module-relative, src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:240). The backend runs with cwd = E2E_PROJECT_DIR (project root; _start_backend sets cwd=str(E2E_PROJECT_DIR), and no os.chdir exists anywhere in src/haute/), but the config is written under rating/ (scripts/run_frontend_e2e_server.py:282-284 -> E2E_PROJECT_DIR/rating/config/quote_input/quotes.json). So a CWD-relative `Path("config/quote_input/quotes.json")` resolves to E2E_PROJECT_DIR/config/quote_input/quotes.json (missing the rating/ segment) and `_config_path.read_bytes()` (line 131) would raise FileNotFoundError. Every other injected block in this file correctly uses __file__-relative paths (e.g. _BROWSER_OPTIMISER_BLOCK line 46 and the same quotes block's own _data_path on line 129), which is what makes this one's bare cwd-relative config path stand out as a defect.
findings.evidence: Fixture (lines 130-149) does: _config_path = Path("config/quote_input/quotes.json"); _v2_config = orjson.loads(_config_path.read_bytes()); _cache_dir = _json_cache_dir(...,'working'); if not is_per_port_cache_valid(...): _cache_dir = _json_cache_dir(...,'committed'); if not is_per_port_cache_valid(...): raise RuntimeError(...); _emit_labels = [...]; _bundle = load_per_port_cache(...); return single-or-dict. Compare production _api_input_template (src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:239-249): _data_path = {portable_path}; _config_path = Path(__file__).parent / {config_path_repr}; ...; return load_v2_api_source(str(_data_path), _v2_config). Cwd proof: _start_backend (line 387-405) uses cwd=str(E2E_PROJECT_DIR); grep over src/haute shows zero os.chdir calls; pipeline_dir()/path resolution (src/haute/routes/_helpers.py:159-167) keeps cwd at project root and only resolves the pipeline file relative to it. Config write location: scripts/run_frontend_e2e_server.py:282-284. The reason this latent bug isn't caught by the api-input-v2-native.spec.ts Preview step is that preview executes the GRAPH via execute_graph -> _build_api_input -> _make_api_source_v2 -> load_v2_api_source (src/haute/_builders.py:464-509), reading config from the sidecar via the route layer, and never imports/invokes the literal quotes() function body from main.py. The body therefore only runs under `haute run`/module-import, where the cwd-relative path breaks.
findings.est_reduction: ~37 lines collapse to a body mirroring production codegen (Path(__file__).parent for the config path + a single `return load_v2_api_source(str(_data_path), _v2_config)`), removing the duplicated cache-resolution logic and the latent FileNotFoundError-on-`haute run` path-resolution bug.
findings.behavior_preservation: For the exercised browser-preview e2e flow, behavior is unchanged because that flow never executes the injected function body (it runs the graph). Replacing the body with the production-equivalent call to load_v2_api_source keeps the file structurally identical for the UI tests while making `haute run` against the scaffold correct and keeping the fixture in lock-step with the real codec.

findings.title: SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers registered after child processes are started, leaving an orphan window if interrupted during startup
findings.description: main() starts the backend (line 507) and Vite (line 508) child processes BEFORE installing the cleanup signal handlers (signal.signal(SIGINT/SIGTERM, _shutdown) at lines 519-520) and BEFORE the try/finally that guarantees _cleanup() (the try begins at line 526). If the operator presses Ctrl+C (or the CI runner sends SIGTERM) during the window between _start_backend()/_start_vite() and the signal-handler registration, the default SIGINT handler raises KeyboardInterrupt which propagates out of main() with no _cleanup() ever running, orphaning the already-spawned uvicorn and/or `npm run dev` processes (each spawned with --strictPort 5173 / port 8000), which then leak and can wedge the next run by holding the ports. Even after handlers are registered, the additional setup before the try block is not covered by the finally. Because the children bind fixed ports, a leaked process turns a transient interrupt into a hard failure on the next invocation.
findings.evidence: Order in main(): backend_proc = _start_backend() (507); vite_proc = _start_vite() (508); processes = [...] (509); def _cleanup()/_shutdown (511-517); signal.signal(SIGINT, _shutdown) (519); signal.signal(SIGTERM, _shutdown) (520); ... try: _wait_for_url(...) ... finally: _cleanup() (526-541). The only cleanup guarantees are the signal handlers (active only from line 519 onward) and the finally (active only from line 526 onward); neither covers the 507->519 window during which both child processes already exist.

functions_reviewed: module-level constants and injected code blocks (_BROWSER_MODEL_BLOCK, _BROWSER_OPTIMISER_BLOCK, _QUOTES_API_INPUT_BLOCK, *_CONFIG, _QUOTES_SAMPLE_DATA)

findings.title: Manual leading './' stripping loop is subsumed by posixpath.normpath
findings.description: In _normalize_repo_path, the `while path.startswith("./"): path = path[2:]` loop preceding `posixpath.normpath(path)` is redundant. posixpath.normpath already collapses any number of leading './' (and '//') segments: normpath('./src/x.py') == 'src/x.py', normpath('././/src/x.py') == 'src/x.py'. The only adjacent case is a path like './../x.py': the loop reduces it to '../x.py', which normpath keeps and the subsequent `normalized.startswith('../')` guard then rejects with CriticalCoverageError; without the loop, normpath('./../x.py') is directly '../x.py' and trips the exact same guard. Removing the two-line loop (and keeping just the strip()+normpath+guard) preserves behavior on all inputs.
findings.evidence: Line 53: `path = raw_path.replace("\\", "/").strip()`; Lines 54-55: `while path.startswith("./"): path = path[2:]`; Line 56: `normalized = posixpath.normpath(path)`. posixpath.normpath collapses leading './' and '//' itself, so the loop never changes the final `normalized` value nor the './..' guard outcome.
findings.behavior_preservation: Identical: normpath subsumes leading './' collapsing for every input; the './..' edge still trips the same startswith('../') guard with or without the loop.

coverage.notes: Verified the script's coverage.py contract against the real artifact (.cache/coverage/backend.json, coverage.py 7.13.4): meta.format==3, meta.branch_coverage==true, per-file summary.percent_statements_covered / summary.percent_branches_covered, and per-file top-level missing_lines / missing_branches (list-of-arcs) all exist exactly as read. Confirmed defensive correctness: bool-before-int guards in _as_percent/_as_missing_*; epsilon tolerance in _evaluate_thresholds is one-directional and correct; missing-critical-file raises loudly (exit 2) rather than silently skipping; _print_success's coverage_files[threshold.path] indexing is safe because _evaluate_thresholds already guarantees every threshold.path is present; truncation off-by-one in _format_missing_* is correct (==limit shows no ellipsis); exit codes 0/1/2 are correct. No correctness bugs, dead code, or swallowed exceptions found. The only reportable item is the redundant leading-'./' loop.

findings.title: `--json` argument is parsed but never read; flag is a complete no-op
findings.description: `_parse_args` defines a `--json` boolean flag (action="store_true"), but `args.json` is never consumed anywhere in the module. `main()` always emits `json.dumps(summary, ...)` to stdout regardless of whether `--json` was passed, and `run_smoke` knows nothing about it. The only formatting toggle is `--pretty`. The help text rationalises it as "the default and is kept as an explicit flag for CI", which makes it intentionally inert, but it remains dead surface: passing or omitting it changes nothing, and a reader/maintainer cannot tell that from the code without grepping the whole file. A Grep for `args.json` across the file confirms zero consumers.
findings.evidence: Line 308-312 defines `--json`. `Grep 'args\.json'` over scripts/memory_smoke.py finds no read site. main() (lines 328-338) builds output solely from `args.pretty` (`indent = 2 if args.pretty else None`) and unconditionally calls `print(json.dumps(summary, indent=indent, sort_keys=True))`. The `--json` value is discarded.
findings.est_reduction: 5 lines (remove the unused argument) or, if kept for CI compatibility, no code reduction but the no-op should be made explicit.
findings.behavior_preservation: Removing the flag changes the CLI surface (callers passing `--json` would error). If CI relies on accepting the flag, behavior is preserved only by keeping it; the finding is that the flag currently has no behavioral effect at all.

findings.title: Windows OpenProcess unnecessarily requests PROCESS_VM_READ alongside PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION
findings.description: The primary `OpenProcess` call requests `PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ` (0x1000 | 0x0010). `GetProcessMemoryInfo` only requires `PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION` on Windows 7 / Server 2008 R2 and later (the legacy requirement `PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ` is the fallback path at line 115). Bundling `PROCESS_VM_READ` into the modern request is unnecessary and strictly narrows the set of processes that can be opened: a target where the caller has query-limited rights but not VM-read rights will fail the first `OpenProcess`, fall through to the legacy `PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ` request (which is even more restrictive), and then return `None`, silently dropping the RSS sample. In this script's own usage the targets are always `os.getpid()` (for peak, line 63) or the wrapper's own child (line 58/242), which grant full rights, so the defect is latent here; but `StdlibMemorySampler` is a reusable public sampler and the over-broad access right is a correctness hazard against any other PID.
findings.evidence: Line 113: `handle = open_process(process_query_limited_information | process_vm_read, False, pid)`. `process_vm_read = 0x0010` (line 93). The modern documented requirement for GetProcessMemoryInfo is PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION alone; VM_READ is only part of the pre-Win7 requirement satisfied by the fallback at line 115. On failure to open, both helpers (`process_rss_bytes`, `process_peak_rss_bytes`) yield `None`, which `_sample_child_rss` (line 186) and the summary then treat as 'unavailable' with no error surfaced.

findings.title: Two-step max over child RSS samples and resource peak is partially redundant
findings.description: The child peak is computed as `child_peak_rss = max(child_rss_samples, default=child_resource_peak)` followed by a conditional `child_peak_rss = max(child_peak_rss, child_resource_peak)`. When `child_rss_samples` is empty, the `default=child_resource_peak` already sets `child_peak_rss` to `child_resource_peak`, and the subsequent `max(child_resource_peak, child_resource_peak)` is a no-op. When samples are non-empty, the second line does the real combine. The intent (overall max of all polled samples plus the resource-reported peak, or None if nothing is available) is expressible as a single filtered aggregation, e.g. `candidates = [*child_rss_samples]; if child_resource_peak is not None: candidates.append(child_resource_peak); child_peak_rss = max(candidates, default=None)`. The current form relies on the `default=` value overlapping the second `max` operand, which is non-obvious and easy to misread as a bug.
findings.evidence: Lines 259-261. Trace: samples=[] -> child_peak_rss = child_resource_peak (default), then line 261 guard fires only if child_resource_peak is not None, computing max(child_resource_peak, child_resource_peak) == child_resource_peak (no-op). samples=[500,300], child_resource_peak=None -> line 261 guard skipped, result 500. samples=[500], child_resource_peak=700 -> max(500)=500 then max(500,700)=700.
findings.est_reduction: ~2 lines net; primarily a clarity improvement removing the overlapping default/max interaction.
findings.behavior_preservation: Equivalent for all input combinations: empty/non-empty sample list crossed with None/int resource peak all yield identical results to the proposed single-aggregation form.

findings.title: Non-strict XPASS perf test is mislabeled as "xfailed" and triggers a false "no tests completed successfully" message, contradicting the JSON summary which labels it "passed"
findings.description:
A perf test marked `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=False)` that unexpectedly PASSES is an XPASS, not an XFAIL. pytest reports it with outcome="passed" and a populated `wasxfail` (empirically confirmed: such a test yields outcome="passed", wasxfail set, and pytest exits 0). The two consumers of this data disagree on its classification, producing inconsistent and misleading output:

(1) `_build_report` line 125 computes `key = "xfailed" if result.wasxfail and result.outcome == "skipped" else result.outcome`. For an XPASS the outcome is "passed" (not "skipped"), so it is bucketed under `"passed"` in the JSON `summary.outcomes`. The artifact therefore claims the test simply passed.

(2) `_budget_violations` line 71 defines `xfailed = [r for r in results if r.wasxfail]`, which INCLUDES the XPASS (its `wasxfail` is truthy). This emits the violation "Performance tests must not be xfailed; expected failures hide perf coverage: <nodeid>" naming a test that actually passed -- a wrong label and a wrong rationale.

(3) `_budget_violations` lines 88-90 require `result.outcome == "passed" and not result.wasxfail` to consider a test successful. The XPASS has `wasxfail` truthy, so it is excluded; if it is the only perf test, the runner additionally emits "No performance tests completed successfully." even though the test ran and passed.

The root cause is that the two code paths use divergent definitions of "xfailed": `_build_report` uses the correct `wasxfail and outcome=="skipped"`, while `_budget_violations` uses just `wasxfail`. Because the repo sets `xfail_strict = true` globally (pyproject.toml:143), a *plain* `@pytest.mark.xfail` that passes becomes a strict XPASS -> outcome="failed" -> caught cleanly via exit code; the inconsistency only surfaces when a test explicitly overrides with `strict=False`, which the global setting does not suppress. The lane still fails overall (exit 1 from the violations), so CI is not silently green, but the emitted reason and the JSON `outcomes` are mutually contradictory and misleading for whoever debugs the failure.
findings.evidence: Empirical probe with pytest 9.0.2: a test `@pytest.mark.xfail(reason=..., strict=False)` whose body asserts True produced report row outcome="passed", wasxfail="...", and `pytest.main` returned EXIT 0. Tracing: _build_report:125 -> key="passed" (outcome != "skipped"); _budget_violations:71 -> wasxfail truthy -> appended to `xfailed` -> message at lines 80-87; lines 88-90 -> `not result.wasxfail` is False -> XPASS excluded from the success check -> if sole test, "No performance tests completed successfully." also fires. pytest's own pytest_report_teststatus (_pytest/skipping.py:315-321) classifies this same report as "xpassed", distinct from both "xfailed" and "passed".

findings.title: Duplicated truncate-to-5 list-formatting for the skipped and xfailed violation messages
findings.description: The blocks building the `skipped` and `xfailed` violation strings (lines 72-79 and 80-87) are near-identical: each joins `result.nodeid` over the first 5 entries, appends ", ..." when more than 5 exist, and formats a message. The shared shape (slice [:5], join on nodeid, conditional ellipsis) could be extracted into a small helper such as `_summarise_nodeids(results, limit=5) -> str` to remove the copy-paste and keep the two messages in sync. This is purely a readability/maintenance cleanup; it does not change observable behavior or output.
findings.behavior_preservation: Identical violation strings before and after; only the construction is factored into a shared helper. Covered by tests/test_perf_suite_script.py::test_budget_violations_fail_when_perf_tests_are_skipped_or_xfailed which asserts the exact message text.

findings.title: _is_stale ignores Vite's root index.html and public/ assets, so edits there ship stale and skip rebuild
findings.description: _is_stale only treats files under frontend/src/ (rglob of *.ts/*.tsx/*.css/*.html) plus a fixed config list (vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, tsconfig.app.json, package.json) as build inputs. But the Vite build (frontend/vite.config.ts: outDir '../src/haute/static', emptyOutDir true) has two additional first-class inputs that are NOT scanned: (1) frontend/index.html — the actual Vite entry HTML at the frontend ROOT (it references /favicon.svg and /src/main.tsx and is transformed into static/index.html), and (2) everything under frontend/public/ (favicon.svg, vite.svg) which Vite copies verbatim into the output. Because src_dir.rglob('*.html') is rooted at frontend/src, the root frontend/index.html never matches, and frontend/public/ is never walked. Consequence, in two places: in initialize() line 50, when HAUTE_BUILD_FRONTEND=1 the rebuild is skipped (returns early) even though the entry HTML or a public asset changed; and in _validate_static_assets() line 85 a normal wheel build passes validation even though the packaged static/ is genuinely older than the changed input. This is exactly the failure the module exists to prevent (module docstring lines 1-6; _validate_static_assets docstring line 77: 'Fail clearly when a wheel build would package missing or stale frontend'). A developer who edits the page <title>, meta tags, favicon, or the script entry in frontend/index.html, then builds a wheel, silently ships the previous build's index.html. Secondary instance of the same gap: tsconfig.node.json (which exists in frontend/) is also absent from the config list, though its build impact is weaker than index.html/public.
findings.evidence: vite.config.ts line 34-35: outDir '../src/haute/static', emptyOutDir true. frontend/index.html exists at frontend root (Vite entry) and references /favicon.svg + /src/main.tsx. frontend/public/{favicon.svg,vite.svg} exist and are copied to outDir by Vite. hatch_build.py:97 src_dir = frontend_dir / 'src'; line 98-101 rglob over src_dir only; line 103 config list omits frontend/index.html and any public/ path. tests/test_hatch_build.py covers only the 'missing assets' path, not staleness of root index.html or public/, so no test catches this.
